text: Let $A=\left \{z\in C:\left |\frac{z+1}{z-1}\right |<1\right \}$ and $B=\left \{z\in C:\arg \left (\frac{z-1}{z+1}\right )=\frac{2π}{3}\right \}$. Then A $\cap$ B is :
options: a portion of a circle centred at $\left (0,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$ that lies in the second and third quadrants only
a portion of a circle centred at $\left (0,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$ that lies in the second quadrant only
a portion of a circle of radius $\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ that lies in the third quadrant only
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\dfrac{z+1}{z-1}\right |<1\Rightarrow |z+1|<|z-1|$

so z is nearer to $-1$ than to $1$: A is the half-plane $\text{Re}(z)<0$.

$\arg \left (\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}\right )=\dfrac{2π}{3}$ means the segment joining $-1$ and $1$ subtends an angle $\dfrac{2π}{3}$ at z, so B is an arc of a circle through $-1$ and $1$.

For $z=iy$ on this arc, $\dfrac{iy-1}{iy+1}=\dfrac{(y^{2}-1)+2iy}{1+y^{2}}$ has argument $\dfrac{2π}{3}$ only when $y>0$, $y^{2}<1$ and $\dfrac{2y}{y^{2}-1}=-\sqrt{3}$, i.e. $y=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. So the arc lies above the real axis and passes through $\left (0,\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$.

The circle through $(\pm 1,0)$ with centre $(0,k)$ and passing through $\left (0,\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$ satisfies

$1+k^{2}=\left (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-k\right )^{2}\Rightarrow k=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}},r=\sqrt{1+\dfrac{1}{3}}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

So B is the arc of the circle centred at $\left (0,-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$ that lies above the real axis, without the end points $\pm 1$.


[IMG]

The part of this arc with $\text{Re}(z)<0$ lies in the second quadrant only.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
The ordered pair (a, b), for which the system of linear equations

3x $-$ 2y + z = b

5x $-$ 8y + 9z = 3

2x + y + az = $-$1

has no solution, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 5 & -8 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & a \end{array}\right |=0\Rightarrow -14a-42=0\Rightarrow a=-3$

Now 3 (equation (1)) $-$ (equation (2)) $-$ 2 (equation (3)) is

$3(3x-2y+z-b)-(5x-8y+9z-3)-2(2x+y+az+1)=0$

$\Rightarrow -3b+3-2=0\Rightarrow b=\frac{1}{3}$

So for no solution $a=-3$ and $b\neq \frac{1}{3}$

text: $\lim _{x\to \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\frac{\sin (\cos ^{-1}x)-x}{1-\tan (\cos ^{-1}x)}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\frac{\sin (\cos ^{-1}x)-x}{1-\tan (\cos ^{-1}x)}$

Let $\cos ^{-1}x=t$

$\Rightarrow x=\cos t$

When $x\to \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, then $t\to \cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\to \frac{π}{4}$

$\therefore$ $\lim _{t\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{\sin t-\cos t}{1-\tan (t)}$

$=\lim _{t\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{\sin t-\cos t}{1-\frac{\sin t}{\cos t}}$

$=\lim _{t\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{(\sin t-\cos t)(\cos t)}{(\cos t-\sin t)}$

$=\lim _{t\to \frac{π}{4}}-\cos t$

$=-\lim _{t\to \frac{π}{4}}\cos t$

$=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

text: Let f, g : R $\to$ R be two real valued functions defined as $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{lll} -|x+3| & , & x<0 \\ e^{x} & , & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$ and $g(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{lll} x^{2}+k_{1}x & , & x<0 \\ 4x+k_{2} & , & x\geq 0 \end{array} \right.$, where $k_{1}$ and $k_{2}$ are real constants. If (gof) is differentiable at x = 0, then (gof) ($-$ 4) + (gof) (4) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ gof is differentiable at x = 0

So R.H.D = L.H.D

$\frac{d}{dx}(4e^{x}+k_{2})=\frac{d}{dx}\left ((-|x+3|)^{2}-k_{1}|x+3|\right )$

$\Rightarrow 4=6-k_{1}\Rightarrow k_{1}=2$

Also $f(f(0^{+}))=g(f(0^{-}))$

$\Rightarrow 4+k_{2}=9-3k_{1}\Rightarrow k_{2}=-1$

Now $g(f(-4))+g(f(4))$

$=g(-1)+g(e^{4})=(1-k_{1})+(4e^{4}+k_{2})$

$=4e^{4}-2$

$=2(2e^{4}-1)$

text: Let $f(x)=2\cos ^{-1}x+4\cot ^{-1}x-3x^{2}-2x+10$, $x\in [-1,1]$. If [a, b] is the range of the function f, then 4a $-$ b is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x\in (-1,1)$,

$f^{'}(x)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}-\frac{4}{1+x^{2}}-6x-2$

Since $\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\leq 1$ and $1+x^{2}\leq 2$, $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\geq 2$ and $\dfrac{4}{1+x^{2}}\geq 2$, so

$f^{'}(x)\leq -2-2-6x-2=-6(1+x)<0$

Thus $f$ is decreasing on $[-1,1]$ and its range is $[f(1),f(-1)]$.

$f(1)=2(0)+4\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )-3-2+10=π+5$

$f(-1)=2π+4\left (\frac{3π}{4}\right )-3+2+10=5π+9$

So $a=π+5$, $b=5π+9$ and

$4a-b=4π+20-5π-9=11-π$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text:

$x^{4}-3x^{3}-2x^{2}+3x+1=0$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{4}-3x^{3}-x^{2}-x^{2}+3x+1=0$

$(x^{2}-1)(x^{2}-3x-1)=0$

Let the root of $x^{2}-3x-1=0$ be $α$ and $β$ and other two roots of given equation are 1 and $-$1

So sum of cubes of roots

$=1^{3}+(-1)^{3}+α^{3}+β^{3}$

$=(α+β)^{3}-3αβ(α+β)$

$=(3)^{3}-3(-1)(3)$

$=36$

text: There are ten boys $B_{1}, B_{2}, ......., B_{10}$ and five girls $G_{1}, G_{2}, ........, G_{5}$ in a class. Then the number of ways of forming a group consisting of three boys and three girls, if both $B_{1}$ and $B_{2}$ together should not be the members of a group, is $___________$.

solution.body:
Number of ways when $B_{1}$ and $B_{2}$ are not together

= Total number of ways of selecting 3 boys $-$ $B_{1}$ and $B_{2}$ are together

$= ^{10}C_{3}$ $-$ $^{8}C_{1}$

= $\frac{10.9.8}{1.2.3}-8$

= 112

Number of ways to select 3 girls $= ^{5}C_{3} = 10$

$\therefore$ Total number of ways = 112 $\times$ 10 = 1120

text: Let f(x) = max {|x  + 1|, |x + 2|, ....., |x + 5|}. Then $\int\limits _{-6}^{0}f(x)dx$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $|x+1|$ critical point, x + 1 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ x = $-$1

For $|x+2|$ critical point, x + 2 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ x = $-$2

For $|x+3|$ critical point, x + 3 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ x = $-$3

For $|x+4|$ critical point, x + 4 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ x = $-$4

For $|x+5|$ critical point, x + 5 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ x = $-$5

 
[IMG]
 

Here maximum function is represent by the dotted line.

$\therefore$ Point of intersection A of line y = $-$x $-$1 and y = x + 5 :

$-x-1=x+5$

$\Rightarrow 2x=-6$

$\Rightarrow x=-3$

$\therefore$ $y=-3+5=2$

$\therefore$ Point $A=(-3,2)$

$\therefore$ $\int\limits _{-6}^{0}f(x)dx$

$=\int\limits _{-6}^{-3}(-x-1)dx+\int\limits _{-3}^{0}(x+5)dx$

$=\left (-\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x\right )_{-6}^{-3}+\left [\frac{x^{2}}{2}+5x\right ]_{-3}^{0}$

$=\left [\left (-\frac{9}{2}+3\right )-\left (-\frac{36}{2}+6\right )\right ]+\left [0-\left (\frac{9}{2}-15\right )\right ]$

$=\left (-\frac{3}{2}+12\right )+\frac{21}{2}$

$=+\frac{21}{2}+\frac{21}{2}$

$=21$

text:
Let the solution curve y = y(x) of the differential equation 

$(4+x^{2})dy-2x(x^{2}+3y+4)dx=0$ pass through the origin. Then y(2) is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(4+x^{2})dy-2x(x^{2}+3y+4)dx=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\left (\frac{6x}{x^{2}+4}\right )y+2x$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}-\left (\frac{6x}{x^{2}+4}\right )y=2x$

$I.F.=e^{-3\ln (x^{2}+4)}=\frac{1}{(x^{2}+4)^{3}}$

So $\frac{y}{(x^{2}+4)^{3}}=\int \frac{2x}{(x^{2}+4)^{3}}dx+c$

$\Rightarrow y=-\frac{1}{2}(x^{2}+4)+c(x^{2}+4)^{3}$

When x = 0, y = 0 gives $c=\frac{1}{32}$,

So, for x = 2, y = 12
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text: If $\sin ^{2}(10^{\circ })\sin (20^{\circ })\sin (40^{\circ })\sin (50^{\circ })\sin (70^{\circ })=α-\frac{1}{16}\sin (10^{\circ })$, then $16+α^{-1}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using $\sin θ\sin (60^{\circ }-θ)\sin (60^{\circ }+θ)=\dfrac{1}{4}\sin 3θ$ with $θ=10^{\circ }$:

$\sin 10^{\circ }\sin 50^{\circ }\sin 70^{\circ }=\dfrac{1}{4}\sin 30^{\circ }=\dfrac{1}{8}$

For the remaining factor, $2\sin 20^{\circ }\sin 40^{\circ }=\cos 20^{\circ }-\cos 60^{\circ }$, so

$\sin 10^{\circ }\sin 20^{\circ }\sin 40^{\circ }=\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 10^{\circ }\cos 20^{\circ }-\dfrac{1}{4}\sin 10^{\circ }$

With $2\sin 10^{\circ }\cos 20^{\circ }=\sin 30^{\circ }-\sin 10^{\circ }=\dfrac{1}{2}-\sin 10^{\circ }$:

$\sin 10^{\circ }\sin 20^{\circ }\sin 40^{\circ }=\dfrac{1}{4}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}-\sin 10^{\circ }\right )-\dfrac{1}{4}\sin 10^{\circ }=\dfrac{1}{8}-\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 10^{\circ }$

Multiplying the two factors,

$\sin ^{2}10^{\circ }\sin 20^{\circ }\sin 40^{\circ }\sin 50^{\circ }\sin 70^{\circ }=\dfrac{1}{8}\left (\dfrac{1}{8}-\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 10^{\circ }\right )=\dfrac{1}{64}-\dfrac{1}{16}\sin 10^{\circ }$

Comparing with $α-\dfrac{1}{16}\sin 10^{\circ }$ gives $α=\dfrac{1}{64}$, so $16+α^{-1}=16+64=80$.

Hence, the answer is 80.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text:
The value of the integral 

$\frac{48}{π^{4}}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\left (\frac{3πx^{2}}{2}-x^{3}\right )\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos ^{2}x}dx$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\frac{48}{π^{4}}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\left [\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )^{3}-\frac{3π^{2}}{4}\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )+\frac{π^{3}}{4}\right ]\frac{\sin xdx}{1+\cos ^{2}x}$

Using $\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(a+b-x)dx$

$I=\frac{48}{π^{4}}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\left [-\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )^{3}+\frac{3π^{2}}{4}\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )+\frac{π^{3}}{4}\right ]\frac{\sin xdx}{1+\cos ^{2}x}$

Adding these two equations, we get

$2I=\frac{48}{π^{4}}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\frac{π^{3}}{2}.\frac{\sin xdx}{1+\cos ^{2}x}$

$\Rightarrow I=\frac{12}{π}\left [-\tan ^{-1}(\cos x)\right ]_{0}^{π}=\frac{12}{π}.\frac{π}{2}=6$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text: Let $S=(0,2π)-\left \{\frac{π}{2},\frac{3π}{4},\frac{3π}{2},\frac{7π}{4}\right \}$. Let $y=y(x)$, x $\in$ S, be the solution curve of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{1+\sin 2x},y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{1}{2}$. If the sum of abscissas of all the points of intersection of the curve y = y(x) with the curve $y=\sqrt{2}\sin x$ is $\frac{kπ}{12}$, then k is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{1+\sin 2x}$

$\Rightarrow dy=\frac{\sec ^{2}xdx}{(1+\tan x)^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow y=-\frac{1}{1+\tan x}+c$

When $x=\frac{π}{4}$, $y=\frac{1}{2}$ gives c = 1

So $y=\frac{\tan x}{1+\tan x}\Rightarrow y=\frac{\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}$

Now, $y=\sqrt{2}\sin x\Rightarrow \sin x=0$

or $\sin x+\cos x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\sin x=0$ gives $x=π$ only.

and $\sin x+\cos x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow \sin \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{1}{2}$

So $x+\frac{π}{4}=\frac{5π}{6}$ or $\frac{13π}{6}\Rightarrow x=\frac{7π}{12}$ or $\frac{23π}{12}$

Sum of all solutions $=π+\frac{7π}{12}+\frac{23π}{12}=\frac{42π}{12}$

Hence, $k=42$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift
